entries.title: U.S., Venezuela strike oil deal. And, the staggering hidden toll of U.S. heat deaths
entries.snippet: The U.S. and Venezuela have entered into an oil deal. And, NPR spent two years tracking heat-related deaths and found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat more than the official counts show.

entries.title: Russia's jet-powered drones bring empty Kyiv supermarket shelves and rattle Ukrainians
entries.snippet: Russian forces relentlessly battered Kyiv and cities in the region around the Ukrainian capital for a fifth straight day, leaving some supermarket shelves bare after repeated strikes on warehouses.

entries.title: Attacks flare between the U.S. and Iran after a monthlong pause
entries.snippet: U.S. threats erupt into attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran retaliates against U.S. targets in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the first exchange of fire since July 29.

entries.title: Hit shows from Edinburgh's Fringe festival are coming to America. Here are our top picks
entries.snippet: The annual "anything goes" performing arts festival featured more than 4,200 performances this year. These are the ones we're still talking about.

entries.title: The U.S. Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
entries.snippet: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

entries.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
entries.snippet: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.

entries.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
entries.snippet: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

entries.title: Singapore is scrambling to stabilize birth rates. Experts see lessons for the U.S.
entries.snippet: Singapore has unveiled a national initiative built entirely around its collapsing birth rate. Some demographers say the plan includes policy ideas that could help American parents.

entries.title: Morning news brief
entries.snippet: Trump says U.S. struck a deal to take control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil, U.S. and Iran resume exchanging strikes, funding at the top of the agenda as House reconvenes.

entries.title: Treasury Department blocks certain journalists from covering G20 meeting
entries.snippet: The New York Times said in a statement that denying American journalists access to an event in the U.S. is "not just another disturbing effort by the administration to undermine independent journalism, but a blatant attempt to evade public scrutiny."

entries.title: Icelandic voters reject a proposal to restart negotiations to join the European Union
entries.snippet: Opponents defeated the measure by a margin of 52.8% to 47.2%, the National Electoral Commission said. The result puts the divisive issue to rest for now.

entries.title: 1 dead and several missing or unaccounted for after Grand Canyon flash flood, park service says
entries.snippet: The flooding Saturday in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, led to more than 60 people being airlifted from the depths of the canyon. The park service asked anyone with details about hikers or campers still unaccounted for to get in touch.

entries.title: Lake Ontario now called Lake America on Google Maps for U.S. users after Trump ordered name change
entries.snippet: Google said in a blog post that the decision was based on its practice of using names assigned by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System, also known as GNIS.

entries.title: U.S. plans to sanction another bank in effort to clamp down on Iran transactions, Bessent tells AP
entries.snippet: "This is going to be financial violence if we have to," Bessent said in the interview. "We are showing people that we know who you are, you know who you are, and this has got to stop."

entries.title: Why Republicans are focusing on transgender issues in competitive 2026 campaigns
entries.snippet: Campaign ads in several midterm elections portray Democrats as "radical" on transgender youth medical care and sports participation. Republicans are leaning on a strategy that proved successful in 2024.

entries.title: U.S. strikes Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in first military action in weeks
entries.snippet: The fighting comes just days after the Trump administration said it would turn its focus to increasing economic pressure — rather than military action — to try to end its war with Iran.

entries.title: Olivia Rodrigo's festival unites women and girls behind nonprofits promoting their well-being
entries.snippet: All-star benefit concerts have proven popular for driving millions of dollars toward everything from refugee relief to pandemic response. But it's been decades since a young artist with Rodrigo's following brought her peers together for gender justice.

entries.title: Karina becomes a Pacific hurricane well away from land and is forecast to become a major storm
entries.snippet: While Karina was expected to stay well away from land, swells from the storm were likely to cause dangerous surf and rip current conditions along parts of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula, the hurricane center said.

entries.title: Lake Ontario to 'Lake America': Who gets to decide what goes on maps?

entries.title: Inside the 24-hour mutiny that threatened Niger's ruling junta
entries.snippet: The unrest culminated in the arrest or killing of dozens of soldiers, some of whom were paraded in front of the cameras live on state television.

entries.title: 1 dead and 5 wounded in a shooting at a rave in Switzerland
entries.snippet: Aargau cantonal police wrote earlier on X that a 22-year-old woman died of injuries at the scene. Four men and one woman, between 24 and 27 years old, were taken to the hospital with injuries ranging from minor to severe.

entries.title: Nepal warns of possible fresh flooding as communities grapple with devastation
entries.snippet: Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones early Sunday as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst hit by Wednesday's catastrophic floods.

entries.title: Ontario premier answers Trump's 'Lake America' with giant 'Lake Ontario' sign
entries.snippet: The 24-by-12-foot sign stands on 6-foot legs, putting its top about 18 feet above the ground — roughly two stories high.

entries.title: NASA's newest space telescope launches on a quest to explore the hidden universe
entries.snippet: The bus-sized telescope — named after the late Nancy Grace Roman, NASA's first chief astronomer — will take more than three months to reach its destination.

entries.title: What we know about Trump's deal giving U.S. access to vast oil reserves in Venezuela
entries.snippet: The answers to questions such as how soon the reserves could be drilled and who will pay to make it happen were not immediately clear. No text of any agreement has been released.

entries.title: 6 months in, Iran's leaders are defying the U.S. and signaling no tolerance for dissent
entries.snippet: Iran's new leaders evince little faith in any agreement with Trump — after coming under attack twice while holding talks — and they may be bracing for another assault once the U.S. replenishes its supplies of interceptors.

entries.title: The Earth is sizzling, but climate isn't a hot topic for Democrats in this year's campaigns
entries.snippet: There has been a national shift in the conversation that is sharp enough for some researchers to coin the term "climate hushing" to describe it.

entries.title: Trump cannot deport students for criticizing Israel, judge rules
entries.snippet: Judge Noël Wise, in a ruling Friday, delivered a victory for the student newspaper at Stanford University, which has said some international students were afraid to speak out because of the deportation threat.

entries.title: Far-right British provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported after his immigration arrest in U.S.
entries.snippet: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said Yiannopoulos was returned to his home country on Friday after being accused of overstaying after entering the U.S. legally in May 2019.

entries.title: Modi-Putin meeting at SCO: Can India-Russia ties hold?

entries.title: Italy extends Schengen suspension with Spain
entries.snippet: Italy's far-right government announced that it will continue to exclude Spanish nationals from the free movement agreement for another 15 days.

entries.title: Nepal floods: A major test for PM Balen's government
entries.snippet: A year after Gen Z-led protests swept Prime Minister Balendra "Balen" Shah to power, deadly floods are testing his government's ability to manage a national crisis.

entries.title: Niger: Failed coup exposes junta's weakness — and Russia's influence
entries.snippet: The failed coup in Niger brings deep divisions within the military to light. As Russia's support highlights the junta's fading influence, soldiers continue to face jihadist attacks, poor equipment and little pay.

entries.title: Swiss police arrest man over deadly rave shooting
entries.snippet: One woman was killed and several others were injured in a shooting at a rave in the Swiss town of Aarau over the weekend. Police say a 43-year-old suspect has been arrested.

entries.title: With multilateralism in decline, what's next for the world?
entries.snippet: The global political architecture is shifting, partly as a result of the actions of US President Donald Trump. As nations search for a new world order, some may gain influence and power, while others have much to lose.

entries.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom

entries.title: Israel signs €3 billion arms export deal with Greece
entries.snippet: Israel said one of its largest ever arms export deals would entail setting up an air defense system for Greece.

entries.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
entries.snippet: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

entries.title: Kenya: Passengers stranded amid airport staff strike
entries.snippet: Airport workers are staging a work slow-down to protest poor working conditions and a lack of support from relevant authorities.

entries.title: Germany news: Police operation in Cologne after shots fired
entries.snippet: Police have cordoned off part of southern Cologne, reporting multiple shots fired at an apparently empty cafe early in the morning. They did not report casualties but were searching the area for a suspect. DW has more.

entries.title: Nepal flood: Death toll crosses 900, thousands still missing
entries.snippet: Rescue teams are racing to reach stranded people, even as nearly 4,800 remain missing. Meanwhile, mass burials have sparked controversy in Nepal.

entries.title: South Korea hands jail term to Unification Church leader
entries.snippet: Han Hak Ja has been convicted on bribery charges after giving the former first lady several luxury gifts. She has denied any wrongdoing.

entries.title: US: Deadly flash flood hits Grand Canyon
entries.snippet: Arizona's Grand Canyon received rainfall of up to 1 inch triggering a flash flood which forced more than 60 people to evacuate. At least one person has died, with over a dozen missing.

entries.title: Google Maps changes Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' in US
entries.snippet: The name change even made its way to some government websites in Canada which pull map data from Google Maps. Meanwhile, Ontario Premier Doug Ford made his position clear by erecting a billboard on the shore of the lake.

entries.title: Iran war: US military strikes Iran's Larak Island
entries.snippet: The attack was the first in over a month. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said they targeted Jordan in retaliation, with Iranian media reporting the UAE was also attacked. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Fact check: Germany's Merz misstates record in ARD interview
entries.snippet: Migration, debt and electric vehicles: Chancellor Friedrich Merz made several misleading claims in his ARD summer interview. DW Fact check reviewed them live.

entries.title: NASA launches first telescope named after female scientist
entries.snippet: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, named after NASA's first Chief of Astronomy, will observe black holes, exoplanets and exploding stars.

entries.title: German churches speak out against AfD ahead of state election
entries.snippet: As the far-right AfD party leads the polls ahead of Sunday’s election in Saxony-Anhalt, Church leaders warn against downplaying its 'ethnonationalist' agenda.
